business.description: Autoline Industries Limited is a leading Indian manufacturer of automotive components and assemblies, established in 1996. It has evolved from a sheet metal stamping company into an integrated engineering and auto-ancillary solutions provider serving major domestic and global OEMs across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, and electric vehicles, while expanding into non-automotive segments.

outlook.statement: Building on the strong foundation of FY 2025-26, we enter FY 2026-27 with greater confidence and a clear strategic direction. Capitalising on the opportunities ahead, we will continue to deepen our partnerships with major OEMs while expanding our reach across automotive and adjacent segments. We will also focus on successfully executing new programmes, strengthening capacity readiness, improving productivity through automation and technology, while enhancing operational efficiencies across our facilities.
Strongly positioned to capitalise on growing opportunities in automotive, non-auto industrial and consumer EV mobility, supporting sustainable growth and long-term value for stakeholders.
AEMPL continued to evaluate opportunities in e-bicycles, battery systems and related mobility applications aligned with evolving market requirements.

The Company expects to achieve sustained improvement in its operational performance through continuous process optimisation, enhanced capacity utilisation, cost efficiency initiatives, product diversification and expansion of its customer base. The management expects these initiatives to support consistent growth in revenue and profitability over the coming years, subject to prevailing market conditions and the overall economic environment. The Company also expects to achieve an annual growth in turnover in the range of approximately 10% to 15% during the ensuing financial year, supported by increased business opportunities, operational efficiencies and continued focus on customer satisfaction.

Going forward, the strategic priority is to convert scale into sustainable, cash-generative growth. The Company will continue to focus on customer and platform depth, capacity utilisation, material and manpower productivity, engineering-led value addition, disciplined capital allocation and stronger working capital management.

Management remains optimistic about future growth opportunities in the EV mobility segment and continues to focus on building scalable operations, distribution capabilities and customer support infrastructure for long-term growth.
AEMPL targeting expansion across key markets including Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Karnataka through phased dealer network growth and market penetration strategies.
Company plans to strengthen online and digital presence through website launch, social media outreach and digital marketing campaigns to support business expansion.

The Indian automobile industry is expected to retain a favourable medium-term growth trajectory, supported by rising incomes, infrastructure development, replacement demand and continued policy support. Growth is likely to remain differentiated across segments, making portfolio balance and programme diversity increasingly important for component suppliers.
According to IMARC estimates, the Indian automobile market could reach approximately US$278.5 billion by 2034, reflecting sustained long-term expansion.

Electric mobility is expected to gather further momentum alongside hybridisation, connected technologies and advanced safety features, increasing engineering intensity and component value while creating new opportunities for suppliers that can adapt manufacturing processes and product portfolios.

Global outlook remains highly sensitive to geopolitical developments, energy-market disruptions, trade-policy shifts and financial conditions. IMF projects global growth of 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027.
India's growth outlook remains underpinned by consumption, investment and infrastructure creation. RBI projected real GDP growth of 6.6% for FY 2026-27.

key_audit_matters: MAT Credit recognition and utilization - Company recognized MAT credit for AY 2011-12 and 2012-13 totaling Rs 1,193.61 Lakhs. During quarter ended June 30, 2025, wrote off MAT credit of Rs 596.81 Lakhs, balance Rs 596.80 Lakhs carried forward. Auditor opines unlikely to be utilized within designated period, overstating total comprehensive income & retained earnings.

Revenue Recognition: Timing of revenue recognition varies due to different customer acceptance terms in sales contracts; revenue is a key performance indicator subject to inherent risk of misstatement

Going Concern: Company returned to profitability since FY 2021-22 but current liabilities exceed current assets; assessment depends on cash flow forecasts with key assumptions on sales volumes, prices, raw material costs, banking facilities, and promoter support

Contingent Liabilities: Evaluation of uncertain tax positions involving assessment proceedings and litigations with direct/indirect tax authorities and other parties; high management judgement supported by independent tax/legal consultants
qualifications_or_emphasis: MAT Credit amounting to Rs 477.19 Lakhs (AY 2011-12) and Rs 716.42 Lakhs (AY 2012-13) scheduled to expire in FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-27 respectively. Company wrote off Rs 596.81 Lakhs during FY 2025-26, remaining Rs 596.80 Lakhs to be written back during FY 2026-27. Management states no impact on cash flows or operational profitability.
Audit trail functionality in Spine HR and SAP B1 - subsequently enabled in SAP HANA and Spine HR
Directors Report for year ended 31st March 2025 did not include explanations on qualifications in Secretarial Audit Report (non-compliance with Section 134(3)(f)(ii) of Companies Act, 2013)
Company has not filed Annual Performance Report of wholly owned subsidiary Koderat Investments Limited, Cyprus for FY 2018-19 to 2024-25 (non-compliance with FEMA regulations)

Resignation of CEO intimated to stock exchanges on 13th August 2025, but letter of resignation and detailed reasons disclosed only on 27th November 2025 (non-compliance with Regulation 30 read with Clause 7(c) of Part A of Schedule III of SEBI LODR Regulations 2015)

Company intimated EGM proceedings on 2nd January 2026 but did not make disclosure to stock exchange(s) about amendments to memorandum of association (non-compliance with Regulation 30 read with Clause 14 of Part A of Schedule III of SEBI LODR Regulations 2015)

Company did not make application for trading approval for listing 42,12,237 equity shares allotted on 27th December 2024 within 7 days from date of grant of listing approval (non-compliance with SEBI Circular dated June 21, 2023); NSE imposed fine of Rs 60,000 plus 18% GST, which was paid

Qualified Opinion: MAT Credit of Rs 596.80 Lakhs carried forward unlikely to be utilized within designated period per tax laws; MAT Credit Asset, total comprehensive income & retained earnings overstated to that extent. Same issue qualified in FY 2024-25.

Emphasis of Matter: Judgment dated February 17, 2026 by Circuit Court of Oakland, Michigan in favor of CJ Holdings North America, LLC holding Company liable for USD 10.38 Lakhs (~Rs 970.23 Lakhs). Net contingent liability disclosed as Rs 530.88 Lakhs (USD 5.68 Lakhs). Based on legal opinion, judgment not directly enforceable in India; requires separate recognition/enforcement proceedings. Opinion not modified.
Audit trail exceptions: SAP B1 used April 1 - May 31, 2025 without audit trail feature; Spine payroll database-level audit trail not enabled April 1 - November 30, 2025
